text:
# Windows across desktops, and a route past a full-screen desktop: design

cc's design for STca1b7f9d59191dfc, on hv decision 13 (fb424e2f), written 23 Nov 2026 at 11:39Z and revised the same day on vc's read (vc decision 111). ic is second reader, on the design and on the code before it lands (vc decision 111, as amended at 13dfd7cc).

The inputs are arngz.log for 23 Nov 2026, the code at main (fb424e2f), Hammerspoon's own window filter source, and ST0026's measurements of 16 Oct 2026.

## What the log shows

### 1. Windows go unnamed, and come back

arngz names a window through two routes only (`nameable`, arngz.lua):

- `hs.window.allWindows()`, which sees the shown desktops;
- `hs.window.filter.default:getWindows()`, which sees what the filter has tracked.

Hammerspoon's own source says why the second route is not enough (`hs.window.filter.forceRefreshOnSpaceChange`, window_filter.lua): "Hammerspoon cannot directly query for windows in Spaces other than the current one; therefore when a windowfilter is initially instantiated, it doesn't know about many of these windows". It learns them "as soon as they're interacted with". The log shows that the filter also loses a window it once had.

| Read (run)                                       | 210770 "gyges"          | 79 "All Connections"         |
| ------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------- | ---------------------------- |
| 11:08:39Z, zeopit saved (20261123T110832Z-6815)  | named, desktop 6 (1894) | unnamed                      |
| 11:10:34Z, rhad saved (20261123T111028Z-56093)   | unnamed                 | named, desktop 7 (6)         |
| 11:16:03Z, auto's which (20261123T111556Z-78812) | unnamed                 | named, desktop 7             |
| 11:16:40Z, auto's end (20261123T111556Z-78812)   | unnamed                 | named, desktop 6, moved here |
| 11:17:25Z, zeopit saved (20261123T111718Z-83575) | named, desktop 6        | unnamed                      |

Both ids stand throughout, so neither window closed. Console's 165, on desktop 7, comes and goes the same way:

- unnamed at 11:08Z and at 11:16:03Z;
- named at 11:10Z, 11:16:40Z and 11:17Z.

Earlier in the day both Screen Sharing windows were named in some reads (eg 10:41:17Z and 10:52:05Z, when gyges was 33933, in full screen).

### 2. An entry with no title took the wrong window

- **The save.** The 11:08Z save named one Screen Sharing window, gyges, on desktop 6. discover pins a window pattern only for an app with more than one window it can claim (`P.desk_from_world`), so it recorded a bare entry: Screen Sharing, desktop 6, 0,0 8x4. vc's copy of zeopit from before shows it.
- **The apply.** At 11:16:10Z, auto's apply of zeopit planned "move window 79 to space 6 ... com.apple.ScreenSharing "All Connections" is on Built-in Retina Display space 7, not space 6", and placed it at 0,0 8x4. A bare entry takes every claimable window of its app, and 79 was the only one named.

### 3. Titles drift

A pattern pinned to one moment's title stops matching when the title changes:

- a browser's title follows its tab;
- a terminal's follows its command;
- Screen Sharing's is its host.

The entry then goes unseen. That is safe, but the window is not arranged.

### 4. Full-screen desktops stop a carry

`P.move_legs` refuses a carry that would pass a non-user space: "a held window cannot be carried into one".

- **rhad's re-run** (20261123T104723Z-91703) ran on the built-in alone. Its live order was `1 3 1431 5 423 121 6 7 1271 1442`, with Screen Sharing's gyges in full screen on 423 and Parallels' kovacs on 121. Four moves were refused, each needing to pass both spaces: Xcode and Devices (1442 to 5), Herdr (1431 to 6), and Teams (5 to 7).
- **The same run's fifth failure** was Appgate's grab. Every point tried on window 166's title bar hit `AXWebArea`, six points over 9.2 s.
- **zeopit's run** (20261123T105242Z-55488) ran plugged in, with live order `1 3 1431 5 7 423 121 6`. One move was refused: Appgate from 6 to 7, past 121 and 423. Above-left and above-right were attached, so a route round through either was there.

## 1. arngz remembers the windows it has named (fault 1)

- **The registry.** `arngz_windows` is a Hammerspoon global, held as `arngz_screens` is. It holds each window arngz has named, by id, with its `hs.window` and the bundle it had when first named.
- **A third route in `nameable`.** After allWindows and filter.default, any id that a space lists and neither route named is named from the registry, with `via = "remembered"`. That needs three things:
  - its reads answer (`describe` already runs under pcall);
  - its app's bundle is the one recorded;
  - a space still lists the id.
  A window that fails any of these leaves the registry and is unnamed, as now.
- **Pruning.** Every named window is put in, or refreshed. An id that no space lists is dropped, so the registry holds only live windows. Pruning runs only in a read where every space's list was read: a space whose list could not be read lists no ids, and its windows are kept (ic's read, 2.2).
- **The log.** The windows records count the remembered, `3 named (1 remembered) of 22`, and mark each one `remembered` in their list of windows, so a read shows which (ic's read, 2.1). help/arngz.md's run log section says so.
- **What it cannot do.** It cannot name a window that arngz has not named since Hammerspoon was last reloaded. A reload drops the registry, as it drops the watcher, and the watcher's start is in the log. Until then, arngz names what the two routes name, and an entry with nothing named is unseen and retried, as now. Bindings (2, below) make that case safe.
- **Measured first** (M1, under Runs). The design rests on a retained `hs.window` still answering, for a window on a desktop its display is not showing: its id, title, frame, application and bundle. The window filter keeps such objects and answers for windows on other desktops, so it is likely. It is not measured. If M1 shows otherwise, this section is withdrawn and 2 carries fault 1 alone.

## 2. An entry keeps the windows it was recorded with (faults 2 and 3)

### The record

Each desk's record is its own JSON file, `$XDG_STATE_HOME/arngz/bindings/<desk>.json`, beside `current` and `own-sizes`, so runs on two desks never write one file. As own-sizes is, it is carried by the CLI, and the engine's P functions compute it. It holds:

- `session`: the boot time and the WindowServer's process id, read by the CLI (`sysctl -n kern.boottime`, `pgrep -x WindowServer`). Window ids start again in a new WindowServer session, so a record from another session is void.
- `desk`: the sha256 of the desk file's bytes. Any edit to the desk voids its record, whoever made it.
- `newest`: the highest window id any space listed when discover --save recorded the desk. Window ids rise within a session (checked in M1).
- `entries`: for each entry path, the window ids it holds.

The CLI passes the record to the engine as `options.bindings`, with the session and the desk file's hash as they are now. P decides whether the record is void, and the log says why. A void record is used as no record.

### One writer

- **Save Desk is the record's one writer.** discover --save writes the record whole: each entry and the window or windows it was recorded from, with `newest`.
  - The engine returns the entries and `newest` in its response.
  - The CLI writes the desk file first. It then adds the session and that file's hash, and writes the record beside its file and moves it over, as own-sizes is written, so no reader ever sees half a record.
- **apply, diff, auto and a plain discover write no record.** A run needs to keep nothing it learns. The ids that rule 5 drops are dropped again by the next run, and a window a bare entry takes above `newest` is taken again by rule 3.
- **A void record stays void until the next Save Desk.** After a reboot or a logout, or once the desk file is edited, plan's rules are today's. A bare entry then takes every window of its app again, so 11:15Z's case can recur until the desk is saved again.
- **A hand edit and the record exclude each other** (ic's read, 3.2). An edit voids the whole record, `newest` with it. Only a Save Desk brings it back, and a save over an existing desk needs `--force` and writes the desk afresh from the screens, which drops the edit.
  - Keeping `newest` through an edit is not taken. With the entries void, a bare entry with a `newest` would take only windows opened since the save: nothing that was there, so it would go unseen.
  - hv's rhad and zeopit carry vc's hand-made Screen Sharing entries. vc has banked them, in ~/Devel/scratch/utilz-vc/desks-titled-20261123/ (rhad f33fc778, zeopit 87fbb597), so the live run's saves lose nothing.
- **arngz delete** removes the desk's record with the desk. Deleting a record by hand is safe: plan's rules are today's until the next Save Desk.
- **help/arngz.md says all of this** (ic's read, 3.1), and its lines that would go false change:
  - an app entry with no `window` takes every window of the app (lines 93 and 131);
  - `unseen` (line 108) also covers an entry whose bound window is listed but cannot be named;
  - the Files and Environment lists gain `bindings/`, and `own-sizes`, which they already lack.

### Two runs and the record

- **What runs beside what.** The engine takes one apply at a time (`arngz_running`, in M.run, arngz.lua): a second apply is refused before it moves anything, with a fix the CLI passes on (arngz:999-1000). Every other verb is answered at once, between an apply's phases. So today a Save Desk clicked during an apply reads windows that the apply is moving, and records them mid-move.
- **A save is refused while an apply runs.** discover --save's request says it is a save (`options.save`). The engine refuses it while an apply runs, as it refuses a second apply: "an apply is running (asked for at ...); save the desk once it has finished". A plain discover, which and diff still answer beside an apply, and write no record.
- **auto's apply is an apply like any other.** It starts only from Menuz's Discover. The display watcher writes the log and starts no run.
- **Two saves of one desk** each write the whole record by a rename, so the last one stands and neither is half written. Saves of two desks write two files.
- **A run that reads beside a save** is safe. A record whose `desk` hash is not the desk file's is void. So an apply that reads the new desk file with the old record, or the old file with the new record, uses today's rules for that one run.

### What plan does with it

1. **Bound windows first.** Each entry first takes its bound windows that are claimable now and unclaimed, before any pattern or bare claim. A bound window is taken whatever its title is now, which answers fault 2 for as long as the window lives. D5's order follows for the rest.
2. **A bound window that a space lists but arngz cannot name makes its entry unseen.** It is retried by `retry_unseen` as now, and said if it stays unnamed. The entry takes no other window in its place.
3. **A bare entry with a `newest` takes only these:**
   - its bound windows;
   - any unclaimed window of its app whose id is above `newest`, a window opened since the save.
   It never takes a window that was there, unrecorded, when the desk was saved. At 11:15Z that rule leaves 79 on desktop 7.
   The rule fails safe: a window it misses is left where it is, unarranged, and never taken by the wrong entry. Two such windows:
   - a window of an app that was hidden at the save, which no space listed then;
   - a window opened after the save with an id at or below `newest`, if ids ever fail to rise (M1 checks that they rise).
4. **A bare entry with no `newest`**, from a desk never saved by discover or a void record, takes every unclaimed window of its app, as today.
5. **A bound id that no space lists, or that is now another app's,** is dropped from the entry. Once an entry has no bound window left, it claims by its pattern, or bare, by these rules.

### Why not the alternatives

- **Pin a pattern for every window, even an app's only one.** That would make every single-window browser entry go unseen at the next tab.
- **Refuse a bare entry for an app with two windows.** That stops the catch-all a person means by a bare entry. A bare entry with a `newest` still catches every window opened since the save.

## 3. A route past a full-screen desktop (fault 4)

### Round through another display (WP3)

Where a move on display A would carry its window past a non-user space, `P.move_legs` looks for a display B. B must have a chain of shared edges to A (`P.route`) and show a user desktop. The fewest crossings wins, then the order of the screens. The legs are the ones a move already has:

1. a switch of A to the window's desktop, if A is not showing it;
2. a drag from A to B, then a readback that the window is on B's shown desktop before the next leg (a drag leg with `check`, as a carry step has);
3. a switch of A to the target desktop, with nothing held, through the full-screen space;
4. a drag from B to A.

- **Why it should work.** Each leg is proven:
  - ST0026's drag across displays landed both ways (16 Oct);
  - a switch with nothing held steps through full-screen spaces, as walk 2 did through 423 and 121.
- **What it leaves.** The move's readback and verdict are as now. B's shown desktop is not changed, since a B that shows a full-screen space is not chosen.
- **In the log.** The op's reason says it goes round through B.
- **On the toast** (ic's read, 4.1). A window that crosses to another display and back needs saying, or it is the unexplained motion hv's first complaint was about.
  - steps_before routes the move from the state the op will see, and gives the step point a `via`, so the toast says "round through <B>". `via` is the desk's name for B, as `display` is the desk's name for A, or the screen's own name when the desk does not describe B.
  - The op routes again when it runs, and the log says so if the two differ.
  - The step row in ST589246c's progress.md gains "`via` (for a move that goes round through another display, the desk's name for it, or the screen's name when the desk does not describe it)", in ic's words (ic's read r2, 1). toast.lua's side is ic's.
- **A round that fails after its first drag** leaves the window on B (ic's read, 4.2).
  - It is not dragged back: after a failure, more gestures risk more.
  - The failure says where it left the window, in ic's words (r2, 1): `<app> not moved to desktop <n> on <A>, and now on <B>'s desktop <m>: <why>`, eg `Appgate not moved to desktop 6 on main, and now on above-left's desktop 2: its frame did not follow the pointer`. <B> is what `via` carries. "now on" rather than "left on", since a desk may name a display "left".
  - It has no fix line: whether a second run helps depends on the why. The next run moves the window on from B.
- **help/arngz.md** says that a move may go round through another display (line 44), that a move past a full-screen window goes round (line 117), and, in its Toasts section, that the step line says "round through <B>" (line 142).

### On the laptop alone (WP4)

There is no B. The question that hv decision 13 answered named two ways round, in vc's words: "On the laptop alone, the only ways round are briefly leaving full screen or driving Mission Control." hv's yes took the thread, not either way, and the choice between them is cc's.

- **Leaving full screen is not taken**, by cc's choice:
  - Both of hv's full-screen apps can resize what they show when they leave full screen: Screen Sharing its remote screen, and Parallels its virtual machine's display.
  - macOS puts the space back where the window re-enters full screen, so the order the person keeps in Mission Control moves.
- **Mission Control is taken if M2 shows it works:**
  1. hold the window as a carry does (`take_hold`);
  2. open Mission Control as `hs.spaces` does, by the Dock's own notification (`hs.spaces.toggleMissionControl`). This needs no shortcut. Mission Control's own shortcut, symbolic hotkey 32, is not set on hv's Mac, so its key is macOS's default, which `P.hotkey` cannot read;
  3. find the target desktop's button in the Dock's Spaces Bar through Accessibility, as `hs.spaces.gotoSpace` does;
  4. drag onto it and let go;
  5. close Mission Control the same way;
  6. read the window's space back.

  It is one leg kind, `mission`, and only for a move whose carry would pass a non-user space with no B. If M2 shows it does not work, WP4 builds only the failure that names the way out, below, and the route is not built.

### Where no route exists (WP4, in every case)

The move fails, naming the way out. It is a failed move, not a refused plan: `P.move_legs` runs when the move does, and its why becomes the move's reason (exec_move, arngz.lua). Today a fix reaches the toast only from a refused plan. So the words change as ic's read (1.1 to 1.5) proposes, the shape ic's and the cases cc's:

- **The fix travels with the reason.**
  - The move's result carries `fix` beside `reason`, and the tally passes the first failure's fix with `first`.
  - The log writes "reason; fix: fix", as it does for a refused plan.
  - Finished shows `Fix:` for a failed or partly run, as for a refused one. toast.lua's side is ic's.
  - The finished row in ST589246c's progress.md changes from "a refusal's fix" to "a refusal's fix, or the first failure's".
- **The reason** leads with the window not moved, by its app's display name, and names every full-screen app the walk would pass, not the first alone: `<app> not moved to desktop <n> on <A>: <app>[ and <app>] <is|are> full screen between desktop <a> and desktop <b>`.
  - Desktops are the desk's ordinals, and <A> is the desk's name for the display, as the step line has them ("moving <app> to desktop <n> on <A>").
  - <a> is the window's desktop and <b> its target, so one template holds when the walk passes full-screen spaces in two gaps (ic's read r2, 2).
- **No window title on screen.** A title can carry a page or a mail subject, and the toast is on screen for anyone looking. The full-screen window's title goes to the log's op record only.
  - The same rule fixes a reason that already breaks it: issue I4eacd29, item 5 of ic's read, filed by ic and closed by this thread's landing on vc's ruling. Today unmovable's reason quotes the window's title (plan.lua:700), and Finished shows it as its problem line. It names the app instead, and the title goes to the log. It says "desktop <n> on <A>", as the toast's other lines do (ic's read of 8620c933).
  - P.plan's reasons name a desk display that has no name "display N", as the step point does, where they said "display nil" (issue Ib12d894, which rides this thread on vc's ruling).
  - A reason names an app as the toast does, by its display name. The world carries each window's app name beside its bundle, read where the bundle is read, so the P functions can name it.
- **The fix fits the case** (ic's read r2, 2):
  - with no other display: `take <it|them> out of full screen, or attach a display, then run it again`;
  - with other displays that share an edge with A, each showing a full-screen space: `take <it|them> out of full screen, or show a desktop on <display>, then run it again`, naming the display the route would take, by the fewest crossings and then the screens' order;
  - with other displays, none sharing an edge with A (two displays that meet only at a corner have no route, since `P.route` needs a shared edge): `take <it|them> out of full screen, or arrange <display> to share an edge with <A>, then run it again`. It is rare, and named so that the advice is never wrong.
- **eg** rhad's Teams move from desktop 4 to desktop 6: `Microsoft Teams not moved to desktop 6 on main: Screen Sharing and Parallels Desktop are full screen between desktop 4 and desktop 6`, then `Fix: take them out of full screen, or attach a display, then run it again`.
- **help/arngz.md** says that, with no route, a move past a full-screen window fails naming the way out (line 117), and that Finished shows the first failure's fix (line 143).

## 4. Appgate's grab point (WP5, left out on hv's word)

- **Left out.** hv decision 15 (vc's record at 37894681, hv's pick read by vc's date -u of 13:03Z on 23 Nov 2026): "Leave it out", vc's option, as vc and cc recommended. A move of Appgate fails at its grab, saying so, as it does today, and hv moves it by hand. M3 is dropped with it.
- **How it came to that.** cc proposed it, since a route needs a grab and zeopit's Appgate move needed both, and vc backed it at first.
  - hv asked: "Is it necessary? Appgate is working fine under arngz as far as I can tell."
  - The log agrees. Appgate was already in place in five runs, and each of the three that had to move it failed: at 10:40Z a pointer move, at 10:48Z no grab point, and at 10:53Z full screen. So it has never been carried, and a press inside a VPN client buys little.
  - vc recommended leaving it out, and cc agreed.
- **If another app shows its class.** ChatGPT's first carry failed at its hold on 23 Nov (issue I7fce35c), and the log does not say whether the point taken lay inside a web area. That issue's fix logs the element under every grab point, so a later failure says. WP5 comes back to hv only if one shows this class.
- **The rule, had hv wanted it**, stands below for the record.

- **One rule.** In a web area, a point is pressed only where its deepest Accessibility element is the web area itself, and only in the window's title strip.
  - Nothing inside a web area is pressed, a plain group included, since a group in a web page is often a clickable div.
  - Appgate is a VPN client, where a stray click could change hv's connection.
- **The title strip** is the band level with the window's zoom button, from the window's top edge to the button's bottom. It is where a native title bar sits.
  - Every point `P.grab_candidates` tries lies in it, level with the middle of the zoom button.
  - A window with no zoom button has no title strip, so no point in its web area is pressed.
- **What it narrows.** Today's hit test takes any plain group (`GRAB_ROLES`), inside a web area too, and WP5 would have taken none there. M3 would have read, without pressing, what lies under the grab points of each window on the shown desktops, so that it was known before the code whether any window arngz holds today is held at a group inside a web area.
- **The proof is the hold.** `take_hold`'s frame readback decides, as it does for every window, since a hit test is not the proof (Dictionary and Stickies, 16 Oct).
- **It would have been measured first** (M3): Appgate's window follows a hold at a point that this rule chooses.

## 5. Windows lost mid-run, and creates that fail at the Dock (WP6, 322a6511, issue I7fce35c)

hv's two applies of homere on 23 Nov 2026, at 13:50Z and 13:56Z, are issue I7fce35c's evidence. vc's ask of the same day puts its fix in this thread, designed here before its code.

### A retry never takes a worse read

- **The rule.** In the unseen wait, `retry_unseen` (arngz.lua:1396-1401) lets any retry plan that does not refuse replace the plan in hand. Now a retry whose world's window filter failed does not replace a plan whose world's filter ran, whatever it plans. The wait goes on, and when it ends, organise runs the plan in hand.
  - The filter is the one route to windows on desktops not shown. Its failure unnames them, which says nothing about the windows. So it is a read that could not be made, as a refusing retry's is.
  - A retry from a world where the filter ran replaces the plan in hand as now, even with more unseen, since that is news about the windows.
- **`P.retry_takes(held_world, world)`** decides it, purely: true, or false and why.
- **The log.** A retry plan that replaces the one in hand is logged as a plan is (`L.plan_pairs`), so the last plan in the log is the one organise runs. A retry not taken is noted, with the filter's error.

### A failed filter says so, with its way out

- When the plan in hand was made from a world where the filter failed, each entry it leaves unseen ends with "Hammerspoon's window filter failed (<error>), so windows on desktops not shown could not be named". Today's words, "the window filter that names windows on other spaces failed: <error>", go.
- Its fix is "run it again; if it fails again, reload Hammerspoon's config (hs.reload() in its console)". The unseen op carries it as `fix`, execute passes it to the result as a report-only op's reason is passed, and the tally passes it to Finished with `first`, as WP4 does for a failed move.

### No false gone

- **The rule.** An app that ran when apply began and reads as not running now is taken as running while a window it had at the start is still listed on a space. The WindowServer lists an app's windows only while the app runs, so the window outweighs the read.
- **The record.** `options.windows_before` holds the ids of the windows named at the start, by app: `P.app_windows` of the inventory's world, set beside `running_before` in PHASE.replan.
- **The log** says when it happens: "<bundle> read as not running, but its window <id> from the start is still listed, so it is taken as running".
- An app that reads as not running with no start window still listed is gone, as now.

### A create that fails at the Dock

- **Now, whatever M2 shows.** A create that fails with "unable to get Mission Control data from the Dock" is not tried again in its callback.
  - Each try asks the Dock to open Mission Control when its group is not there (spaces.lua:100 and 723), so a second try while it is still opening can close it again.
  - `P.space_error_kind` names it `dock`, and `attempts`' stop ends the tries at once, as it does for `gone`.
  - Its reason says the Dock did not open Mission Control for Hammerspoon, and its fix is "add the desktop in Mission Control by hand, then run it again".
  - It binds every display for the run, not only its own: no other desktop is asked for in that run, on any display, since Mission Control is one for all of them and prepare asks for every create in one callback (vc's ruling on 4ce6eec1). The later creates say so, with the same fix.
  - This narrows 0135's fix, which tries every create four times. The Dock's failure was never ridden out: not in either of hv's runs, nor in 0135's run 35.
- **After M2.** M2 opens Mission Control as `addSpaceToScreen` does, and records whether its group appears within 2 s.
  - If it appears, arngz opens Mission Control itself in prepare, and looks for its group in later callbacks, for up to 5 s, before it asks for the desktop. `addSpaceToScreen` then finds it open, and does not ask the Dock again.
  - If it does not, nothing more is built, and the failure above is the answer.

### The grab point in the log

- Every hold notes, before it presses, the point and the element under it, and whether a web area holds that element, eg "carry: pressing window 143089 at 1061,52 on an AXGroup inside a web area". So the next failed hold says whether it is WP5's class (section 4).
- The note is the log's alone. A failed hold's reason is unchanged.

### Finished says what the first is

- The tally's `first` stays the words of the first counted entry not placed, in desk order. Beside it, `first_outcome` says what that entry was: failed, unseen or skipped. Finished carries it, so the toast can show an unseen first as not found, never under "failed". It is absent when `first` is a refusal's or a failed run's words.
- The finished row in ST589246c's progress.md gains `first_outcome` ("failed", "unseen" or "skipped": what the entry first names was, in the tally's own keys), in ic's words, on cc's word and ic's.
- toast.lua's side is ic's. A partly run's reason line takes its label from COUNTS, the table that words the counts, so the label and the count cannot disagree: "Not found: <first>", "Failed: <first>" or "Skipped: <first>". With no `first_outcome`, or one toast.lua does not know, it shows the words alone, as today. The failed head is unchanged, since its first is the run's own error (ic's read of section 5).

### What WP1 adds

WP1's registry, if M1 holds, names the windows of both runs: the 17 that the filter's raise unnamed, and the six lost after the failed create. WP6 does not wait on it.

## What stays

- D5's order, for what bindings do not claim. D11, which leaves full-screen windows alone.
- The carry wherever no non-user space lies on the walk, and every readback.
- The unseen retry, and patterns as discover pins them.
- A move with no route fails, as now, in the words of section 3.

## Work packages

- **WP1 (026eadfc), arngz remembers the windows it has named.** The registry and the third route in `nameable`, the remembered counted and marked in the windows records, and help. S.
- **WP2 (b9d4e976), an entry keeps the windows it was recorded with.** The bindings record, one file per desk and written by Save Desk alone, with plan's five rules, the engine's refusal of a save while an apply runs, and help. M.
- **WP3 (dca427e7), round a full-screen desktop through another display.** In `P.move_legs`, with the drag's `check`, the step's `via`, a failure that says where it left the window, and help. S.
